title: Futures vs Stocks
hook: Futures aren't stocks. The rules are different. Let's break it down.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain why futures fit a movement-based framework better than stock ownership does.

blocks.heading: Stocks are about ownership. Futures are about movement.

beats.heading: The cleanest way to separate them
beats.body: With stocks, you're buying ownership in a company. With futures, you're trading a contract based on price movement — no company stake involved.

beats.heading: Why it matters here
beats.body: That difference changes how you think about direction, risk, and flexibility — and it's why Dayli ICC makes more sense in futures.

blocks.heading: What's wrong with her plan?
blocks.scenario: A new trader says: "I'm going to hold this futures contract for 10 years, like a stock."

options.label: Futures contracts expire — they aren't built for indefinite holding the way stock ownership is
options.feedback: Exactly — that plan misunderstands what a futures contract actually is.

options.label: Nothing's wrong with it
options.feedback: Futures contracts have expiration dates and aren't long-term ownership vehicles.

left.label: Stocks
points: You own a piece of a company

right.label: Futures
points: A contract based on price movement

blocks.quote: Futures naturally fit long and short thinking — that flexibility is exactly why this training is built around futures, not stocks.

questions.question: A trader wants to profit from a short-term price move without caring about long-term company ownership. Which instrument type is built for that, and why?
options: Futures — a futures contract is based purely on price movement, not ownership
Stocks — stock ownership was always designed for short-term moves
Neither — instrument choice has nothing to do with that goal
questions.why: Futures contracts are built purely around price movement, with no ownership stake.

questions.question: Futures thinking focuses on direction and:
questions.why: Futures are built around price movement, not the ownership perks that come with stock.

takeaways: Stocks are ownership. Futures are a contract on movement.
Futures contracts expire — they aren't a buy-and-hold-forever vehicle.
Movement-based thinking is exactly why futures fit this framework.
remember: You're not buying a piece of a company. You're trading movement.
